info.title: Airwave Public API
info.description: Read your self-hosted Airwave server's live data (guide, channels, now-watching) and subscribe to webhooks. Authenticate with an API key from Settings → API Keys, sent as either `X-API-Key` or `Authorization: Bearer`.

name.description: The server's friendly display name (editable in Settings → General).

uptimeSeconds.description: Seconds since this server process started.

workflowEngine.description: The AI lineup workflow engine is enabled on this server.

features.description: Optional server features a consumer might branch on.

eventTypes.description: Subscribable webhook event types (empty until webhooks ship).

definition.description: Present only with ?include=definition. The channel's authoring internals (filter tree / membership sources / manual items, plus ordering + strategy). Opaque and NOT covered by the API stability guarantee.

example.name: 90s Sitcoms
example.description: Comfort-watch classics from the decade of the sitcom.

ChannelMode.description: How the channel's pool is built: a metadata filter, Plex playlists/collections (membership), a hand-picked list (manual), or a mix.

ratingKey.description: The Plex media ratingKey, or null (e.g. an interstitial bumper).

artworkUrl.description: Ready-to-use, tokenless artwork URL (the portrait poster). Host-relative, so prepend your server's base URL and use it directly in an / entity_picture. Null when there's no artwork (e.g. a bumper). Backed by GET /channels/{channelId}/artwork/{ratingKey}.

offsetSeconds.description: Seconds elapsed into the current slot (present on the current slot only).

disabledAt.description: Set if the endpoint was auto-disabled after repeated failures.

secret.description: The signing secret (whsec_...). Shown ONCE, here only. Store it now — you can't retrieve it again.

eventId.description: Also sent as the webhook-id header (consumer dedupe).

get.description: This server's identity (product, version, install id, display name), current time, uptime, and live counts (channels, packages, active viewers). The one-stop endpoint for a Home Assistant sensor.
What this public API supports on this server: API version, optional server features, and whether webhooks and the SSE event stream are available. Lets a consumer degrade gracefully.
Every channel you can access, in guide order. Add ?include=definition for authoring internals.

get.summary: Get a channel by its guide number

get.description: The currently-airing slot (with its live offset) and the one after it.

endsAt.description: When the materialized schedule runs out; ISO-8601 UTC.

get.description: The channel's upcoming programs over the next N hours (default 3, max 24).
Packages that contain at least one channel you can access.

get.summary: Get a package and its channels

get.description: Every accessible channel with its programs over a window. The marquee endpoint for a full EPG view.

get.summary: What's on right now (one row per channel)
get.description: A compact now/next per channel — ideal for a Tidbyt or a small dashboard.
Who's watching what right now (heartbeated within the last 30 seconds).
The number of active watch sessions — the cheapest sensor for 'is anyone watching'.
A friendly, compact view of what each active viewer is watching.

Streams program artwork from the channel's Plex source. No API key or Plex token needed, so the URL drops straight into an , a Home Assistant entity_picture, or a Tidbyt. `kind` selects the poster (portrait, default), the background (landscape fanart), or the item's own thumb. Prefer the `artworkUrl` a program or session gives you.
